**567 VA OIG recommendations are open in this dataset. The data is current as of November 4, 2026, which is 6 days old and not stale.**

**Why OIG's own dashboard shows a different number:** OIG's [data dashboard](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/data-dashboard) lists **586** open. I checked the two row by row and they hold exactly the same open recommendations. The 19 extra on OIG's side are blank rows on its pages. The data passed its reconciliation check on November 4, 2026, and the gap is within the accepted tolerance.

**How old the open items are, by publication year:**

| Year published | Open recommendations | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 | 369 | 103 |
| 2025 | 118 | 47 |
| 2024 | 24 | 14 |
| 2023 | 24 | 8 |
| 2022 | 13 | 7 |
| 2021 | 18 | 9 |
| 2018 | 1 | 1 |

Most open items (about 86%) come from 2025–2026 reports. The 2018 item is the oldest. The report counts here include only reports with at least one open recommendation.

OIG also groups open items by age: 409 are under 1 year, 160 are 1–5 years, and 17 are over 5 years. Those figures add up to OIG's total of 586, not to the 567 in this data.

**Caveats:**
- The year breakdown can be read more than one way. Having more open items from recent years may just mean newer recommendations haven't had time to close. It could also reflect changes in how many reports OIG publishes, its inspection protocols, or where it focuses.
- None of these open recommendations has a closure date yet, so I can't say from this set how long they take to close.
- These are totals across all reports, so no single report is the source. The underlying list is at [vaoig.gov/recommendations-all](https://www.vaoig.gov/recommendations-all).

For context, the dataset holds 15,649 recommendations in total: 14,925 closed as implemented, 157 closed as not implemented, and 567 open.

OIG made **148 recommendations** in Healthcare Facility Inspection reports published in 2026, and **80 of them (about 54%) are still open**.

The data is current as of **November 4, 2026** (6 days old, not stale), so reports published later in 2026 aren't included yet.

| Status | Recommendations |
|---|---|
| Open | 80 |
| Closed, implemented | 68 |
| Closed, not implemented | 0 |
| **Total** | **148** |

**What to keep in mind:**
- **Number of reports:** The data shows 61 Healthcare Facility Inspection reports in 2026, but that figure includes reports with no recommendations. The 80 open recommendations come from 31 reports.
- **Time to close:** For the 68 closed recommendations, the median time to close is 0 days. That means at least half were closed the day the report came out, probably because the facility fixed the problem during the inspection. It isn't a typical time to close.
- **Why so many are open:** Many of these reports came out only months ago, so a high open share is expected.
- **Gap with OIG's dashboard:** For all reports, OIG's dashboard shows 586 open recommendations and this data shows 567. A row-by-row check found the same recommendations in both places. The gap is 19 blank rows on OIG's pages, so your 2026 count may be slightly off from what OIG's dashboard shows.
- **Comparing years:** If you compare these numbers to other years, a change can mean facilities improved. It can also mean OIG changed its inspection methods, how many reports it publishes, or what it focuses on.

These are totals across many reports, so no single report is the source. They come from OIG's recommendations data at https://www.vaoig.gov/recommendations-all. I can list the reports with open recommendations, with their report numbers and links, or break the open items down by facility or VISN.

**2015 had the most: 1,914 recommendations**, from 396 reports published that year. Data is current as of 2026-11-04, which is 6 days old.

**Next-highest years:**
| Year | Recommendations | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| **2015** | **1,914** | 396 |
| 2014 | 1,670 | 217 |

Since 2021, yearly totals have been lower, between about 600 and 1,100. 2026 shows 631 so far, but the year isn't over.

- **Early years are missing.** Before 2012 the data shows almost no recommendations, even though OIG published many reports then (for example, 207 in 2012 and 187 in 2011). That probably means OIG's public recommendations list doesn't go back that far, not that OIG made no recommendations. So 2015 is the peak among the years this data covers.

A check found this gap within tolerance, so it won't change which year is highest. Separately, OIG's dashboard shows 586 open recommendations and this data shows 567. The 19-item difference is blank rows on OIG's pages. A row-by-row comparison found the same recommendations in both.
- **Year-to-year changes have more than one explanation.** A drop in the count could mean fewer problems. It could also reflect changes in how OIG inspects, how many reports it publishes, or what it focuses on. The 2015 peak lines up with OIG's highest report volume in this data (396 reports).

By this count, suicide prevention is **not growing**. Reports with a recommendation that mentions "suicide" fell sharply from 2024 to 2025. The drop mostly reflects a change in which inspection programs OIG ran, so it doesn't show that OIG cares less about suicide prevention.

**The counts** (data as of 2026-11-04, 6 days old, so current)

| Year published | Reports with a recommendation mentioning "suicide" | Matching recommendations | Still open |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | **56** | 98 | 0 |
| 2025 | **11** | 19 | 6 |

For scale, the data has 180 OIG reports published in 2024 and 155 in 2025. Those totals include reports with no recommendations, so treat these shares as rough: about 31% of 2024 reports had a matching recommendation, versus about 7% in 2025. OIG's total output fell a little, but the suicide-related count fell much more.

**What explains most of the drop**

Splitting the matching recommendations by report type:

- **2024:** 55 of the 98 came from Comprehensive Healthcare Inspection Program (CHIP) facility inspections. Another 18 came from hotline inspections, 15 from Vet Center inspections, 8 from national reviews and 2 from mental health inspections.
- **2025:** none came from CHIP. CHIP was replaced by the Healthcare Facility Inspection program, and none of its recommendations matched. The 19 matches came from mental health inspections (9), Vet Center inspections (5), national reviews (3) and hotline inspections (2).

So most of the decline comes from retiring CHIP, which often produced suicide-related recommendations. Outside CHIP, matches fell from 43 recommendations to 19.

**What these counts can show**

- How often the word "suicide" appears in OIG recommendations each year.
- Which report types those recommendations came from.
- Their status: all 98 from 2024 are closed as implemented. 6 of the 19 from 2025 are still open, 3 of them Vet Center items that have been open for more than a year.

**What they cannot show**

- **Whether suicide prevention got better or worse.** A falling count can mean facilities improved. It can also mean OIG changed its inspection methods, published fewer reports or shifted its focus. The program switch is the clearest example here.
- **OIG's overall attention to the topic.** This counts only recommendations. Reports can discuss suicide in findings that led to no recommendation, and some 2025 recommendations may cover suicide risk in other words, such as "suicidal," "safety plan" or "lethal means." A keyword search would miss those.
- **A trend.** Two years is two data points. You'd need a longer series, ideally split by program, to call anything a trend.
- **How serious the problems were.** Recommendations differ in scope, so a count says nothing about severity.
- **Whether target dates were met.** A target date is the facility's own estimate, and OIG may close a recommendation months after the work was done. A late closure or an item open past its target doesn't prove a facility missed its commitment.

These are totals across many reports, so no single report is the source. Each recommendation can be looked up at https://www.vaoig.gov/recommendations-all. Next steps could be a 2019–2025 series for a longer view, or the same count limited to the "Suicide Prevention" topic label. OIG applied that label to only about a quarter of reports, so the label count would undercount.

**The median is 179 days, a little under six months.** That covers VBA recommendations that have been closed. The data is current as of **2026-11-04**, six days old and not flagged stale.

| Measure | VBA |
|---|---|
| Recommendations naming VBA | 966 (923 closed, 43 open) |
| Closed recommendations with a usable closure date | 914 |
| **Median days to close** | **179** |
| Middle half of closures (25th to 75th percentile) | 134 to 312.5 days |
| Closed the day the report came out | 110 |
| Closed as not implemented | 26 (2.8%) |

**What the number measures**
- It's the time from when OIG published the report to the closure date shown on OIG's site.
- **It's not the time VBA took to do the work.** The closure date seems to record when OIG closed the recommendation after reviewing VBA's evidence, which can be months after the work was finished. So 179 days likely overstates how long the fixes themselves took.
- **It only counts closed recommendations that have a closure date.** It uses 914 of the 923 closed ones. About 6% of closed recommendations, mostly from 2013 to 2016, have no closure date on OIG's site.
- **It leaves out the 43 that are still open.** Their median age is 161 days, 17 have been open more than a year, and the oldest has been open 1,567 days. Since slow cases still open aren't counted, the median may come out lower than it will be once they close.
- **It counts same-day closures as zero days.** 110 were closed the day the report came out, probably because they were fixed before publication. That pulls the median down a little.
- **It includes recommendations shared with another office.** A recommendation naming more than one office counts for each. The same search also returned 11 OIT recommendations (median 330 days) and 5 VHA recommendations (median 71 days), but those groups are small and overlap with VBA's.

**What the number can't tell you**
It doesn't show whether VBA met its own target dates. A target date is VBA's own estimate, and OIG's closure can come months after the work is done. A recommendation that closed after its target date, or is still open past it, doesn't prove VBA missed its commitment.

These are totals across many reports, so no single report is the source. The data comes from OIG's recommendations page: https://www.vaoig.gov/recommendations-all. OIG's dashboard shows 586 open recommendations across all offices, while this data has 567. A row-by-row check found the same recommendations in both, and the gap is 19 blank rows on OIG's pages.

OIG made **two recommendations** in report **25-00193-155**, *Healthcare Facility Inspection of the VA El Paso Healthcare System in Texas*, published July 16, 2026. You can see it at the [report page](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-el-paso-healthcare-system) or the [PDF](https://www.vaoig.gov/sites/default/files/reports/2026-07/vaoig-25-00193-155_final.pdf).

1. **Environment of care:** "Executive leaders ensure staff maintain a clean and safe environment."
2. **Primary care:** "The Medical Center Director ensures providers complete secondary toxic exposure screenings within 30 days."

**The clean and safe environment recommendation (#1):**
- **Did the facility concur?** Yes.
- **Target date:** January 29, 2027.
- **Status:** Still open, with no closure date.
- **What the facility said it would do (report p. 12):**
  - Environmental Management Services staff clean all areas at least daily.
  - Restroom cleaning is recorded on a log on the back of each restroom door. Public restrooms have a posted phone number to call if they aren't clean.
  - A staff member checks busy public restrooms throughout each business day.
  - It put 24 cleaning procedures in place and trained staff on them by June 2, 2026.
  - The Chief of Environmental Management Services checks cleanliness daily, and the Associate Director inspects weekly.
  - All employees were told about their part in keeping the facility clean at a town hall on June 2, 2026.

OIG also noted some problems it did not make recommendations about, because the facility had already fixed them by December 2025. Clean supplies had been stored in soiled utility rooms, expired masks were found in a storage room, and an emergency alert system could only be reset from the locked police station.

**About the data:** It's current as of November 4, 2026 (6 days old, not stale). A general note from the data source: OIG's dashboard shows 586 open recommendations, but this data has 567. A row-by-row check found the same recommendations in both, and the gap is 19 blank rows on OIG's pages. That doesn't affect this report.

The most common recurring finding under the Healthcare Facility Inspection program is about **communicating test results to providers and patients**. It appears in 21 of the 112 reports in scope. El Paso is **not** in that group. Its inspection report was cited for a different recurring issue, keeping the environment clean.

**The most common finding: test-result communication (cluster 260)**
- The recommendation reads: *"The Chief of Staff and Associate Director for Patient Care Services develop workflows that describe how each team member participates in the process to communicate test results, in accordance with Veterans Health Administration Directive 1088(1), Communicating Test Results to Providers and Patients."*
- **How common:** 26 recommendations across 21 of 112 reports, which is about 19%. All were issued in 2026.
- **Status:** 17 of the 26 are still open, and none were closed as not implemented.
- **Time to close:** only 9 have a closure time on record, and the median is 0 days. That most likely means they were closed the day the report came out, so it says nothing about how long the fix takes.
- **The same theme shows up elsewhere:** a separate group (cluster 261) has 12 more reports, from 2025–2026. Those ask leaders to make the facility's test-result policy and workflows meet VHA requirements and to monitor whether patients are told their results. Its median time to close is 256 days, based on 9 closed items. Because one theme can be split across groups like this, 21 reports is a minimum for this theme, not a full count. The two groups may overlap, so they can't simply be added together.
- The next most common groups are cleaning to reduce infection risk (11 of 112 reports), stable leadership at the facility, set by the VISN Director (9 of 112), and keeping patient care areas clean and safe (9 of 112).

**VA El Paso Healthcare System (station 756, VISN 17)**
Its inspection report is [25-00193-155](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-el-paso-healthcare-system), published July 16, 2026, from an inspection on January 14–16, 2025. It made two recommendations, and neither is about test results:
1. *"Executive leaders ensure staff maintain a clean and safe environment."* This is **open** and the facility agreed with it. The target date is January 29, 2027. It belongs to a smaller recurring group about the cleaning theme (cluster 270), found in 4 reports.
2. *"The Medical Center Director ensures providers complete secondary toxic exposure screenings within 30 days."* This is **open** and the facility agreed. The target date is December 31, 2026. It doesn't match any recurring group.

El Paso also has no repeat findings on record. Repeat findings means the same standard recommendation cited in more than one of a facility's reports. OIG inspects against a standard protocol, so a repeat would show the issue was cited again, not that nothing was done in between. Only recommendations that belong to a recurring group are compared.

**About these numbers**
- A recurring group is made of recommendations with matching or similar wording. That suggests a shared issue but doesn't prove a common cause.
- Not appearing in a group means OIG didn't cite that facility for the issue in that report. It isn't a rating of the facility, and this data doesn't rate or rank facilities.
- If El Paso has no response on record for a finding, that only means none was pulled from the report. It doesn't show that the facility failed to respond or that anything is overdue.

**Data as of November 4, 2026** (6 days old, not stale). OIG's dashboard shows 586 open recommendations, while this data has 567. A row-by-row check found the same recommendations in both; the gap is 19 blank rows on OIG's pages.

- **Estimated window: around January 16, 2028.** This is an estimate, not a schedule. It's the end date of the last inspection (January 16, 2025) plus about three years, based on the program's roughly three-year cycle. Reports usually come out months after the inspection itself.

**What the facility said it is doing:**

- **Toxic exposure screenings:** zero screenings overdue past 30 days as of June 1, 2026. A written procedure is still being developed. Monthly reports to the clinical council began in June 2026, with a goal of six months in a row at zero overdue.

**Problems the 2026 report found that got no formal recommendation** because the facility fixed them first. These are still worth rechecking:
- Clean and dirty items stored together in the primary care and women's health clinics

This is from 112 recent reports in scope, listed by how common each finding is, not by how serious it is.

1. **Written workflows for sharing test results with providers and patients** (21 of 112 reports). Examples: Shreveport, 26-00057-170 ([link](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-shreveport-healthcare)), and Madison, 25-00254-277 ([link](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-william-s-middleton-memorial)).

- Peer actions are the closest matches by wording and meaning, so not every example fits its group exactly. Target dates are each facility's own estimate, not a measure of missed deadlines.
- Similar wording suggests a shared issue but doesn't prove a common cause, and no single group gives a full count for a topic.

- This summarizes public records only. It doesn't rate or rank the facility.

**Where to focus:** close out the four open items, especially the two data-center items from 2023, which have no target dates recorded. Make sure the fixes made before the 2026 report are holding.
